html:
The Alsea were a people of the central Oregon coast, living in villages around Alsea Bay and along the lower Alsea River, near today's Waldport. Their language, Alsea, and that of the Yaquina to the north formed a small family of their own. It is now extinct.

They lived from salmon, shellfish and sea mammals, in cedar plank houses by the water. In 1855 their land became part of the Coast Reservation, which the government then shrank in the 1860s and 1870s. Survivors became part of the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians. Neighbours: Siuslaw and Tillamook.
